info.title: TrueCalc Pro command API
info.description:
This document maps Studio's own hosted-REST convention (`packages/api-contract/src/openapi/build-document.ts`: POST /workbooks, POST /workbooks/{id}/commands, GET /workbooks/{id}, GET /workbooks/{id}/cells/{a1}) onto this crate's actual capabilities today.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: this crate has no document-handle/session registry yet (see src/mcp_server.rs's own "one process, one document" scope note — the same boundary). The realistic v1 surface is therefore a single, session-less POST /commands rather than Studio's /workbooks/{id}/commands — a scoped, documented decision, not an oversight, the same posture this crate already takes for file:export/file:import's deferred xlsx arm. A real hosted adapter with a document-handle registry is tracked separately.

post.summary: Apply a batch of wire commands to the process's one document
post.description: Session-less v1 batch endpoint — see info.description for why this is not /workbooks/{id}/commands.

200.description: One outcome per batch entry, in request order — each this crate's CommandOutcome<Value> success shape or EnvelopeFailure shape. NOT modeled as JSON Schema here: envelope.rs's types (CommandOutcome/EnvelopeFailure) do not derive JsonSchema today (unlike CellRange) — left as a loose placeholder rather than a fabricated schema, a scoped follow-up.

FormatFillColorPayload_Color.description:
A CSS colour string — `#ff0000`, `#fff2cc`, `rgb(…)`, a named colour.

# Why this is not a parsed colour

`schema.ts`'s validator for `color`/`fill` is `typeof v === 'string'`, full
stop. Studio's own writers only ever emit `#rrggbb`, and its
conditional-format wire validator *does* enforce a `HEX_COLOR` pattern —
but the plain cell format's does not, and a document containing
`color: "rebeccapurple"` loads today.

Parsing to an RGB triple here would therefore make documents that open stop
opening, and would re-serialize `"#FF0000"` as `"#ff0000"` — different
canonical bytes for a document nobody edited. So this is a validated
*string*, and the one thing it rejects is the empty string, which is not a
colour and which TypeScript only ever tolerated because
`isEmptyFormat` treated it as "no colour at all" (see
[`CellFormat::is_empty`](super::CellFormat::is_empty)).

FormatSetFontSizePayload_FontSize.description:
A font size in points.

# The one place this is stricter than TypeScript

`schema.ts`'s validator is `typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v)` —
so `fontSize: 0` and `fontSize: -8` are *accepted* by the importer. Neither
renders as anything, and neither survives an edit: `isEmptyFormat` treats
`0` as falsy, so the first format touch on such a cell deletes the whole
record.

This type refuses both. Nothing is lost, because the wire reader
([`super::wire`]) drops a non-positive size to absence rather than failing
the load — the identical outcome to the collapse the TypeScript already
performs, reached deliberately instead of by accident.

FormatSetBordersPayload_BorderEdge.description:
One drawn edge: how it looks.

`schema.ts`'s `isBorderEdge` requires **exactly** these three keys — an edge
with a fourth is rejected rather than trimmed, and one missing `color` is

FormatSetBordersPayload_Color.description:

`schema.ts`'s validator for `color`/`fill` is `typeof v === 'string'`, full

opening, and would re-serialize `"#FF0000"` as `"#ff0000"` — different
canonical bytes for a document nobody edited. So this is a validated

negative clockwise ("down").

`0` is the identity and is **not** a distinguishable state — `format.ts`
says so outright ("`undefined` (or `0`) = no rotation"), so

rotation of nothing.

# Why `f64` and not an integer

Sheets' UI only offers whole degrees and five presets (±45, ±90, 0), so an
`i8` is tempting and would make this type `Copy + Eq + Hash` for free.
`schema.ts`'s validator is `Number.isFinite(v) && v >= -90 && v <= 90`,
though — **not** `Number.isInteger` — so a document carrying `rotation:
45.5` loads today, and an `i8` port would refuse to open it. Narrowing an
accept-set is a migration, not a translation.

FormatSetDecimalsPayload_Decimals.description:
A fixed decimal-place count for a [`NumberFormat`].

# `Decimals(0)` is a value, not an absence

This is the type that carries the port's one deliberate behaviour change.
In TypeScript `decimals` is `number | undefined` and
`isEmptyFormat` — `Object.values(f).every(v => !v)` — reads `0` as falsy, so
setting zero decimal places on an otherwise-unformatted cell deletes the
cell's whole format record and the cell falls back to **automatic, which is
two decimal places**. Studio's own write-observer classifies that as
`blocked` and calls it "the exact false success R10 names"
(`api-contract/src/observe-writes.ts:280-320`).

`Option<Decimals>` cannot express that confusion: `Some(Decimals(0))` and
`None` are different values, and reproducing the collapse would mean writing
it deliberately. See [`CellFormat::is_empty`](super::CellFormat::is_empty)
for the full decision.

A cell's grid-owned presentation.

Every field is optional and absence is meaningful — see each field's doc for
what absent means, because it is not "false" everywhere: an absent `align`
is *automatic* (type-based), an absent `valign` is *bottom*, and an absent
`decimals` is *two*, not zero.

# Equality and hashing

Derives `Eq` and `Hash`, matching `truecalc_workbook::Workbook`, so a
document can be hashed as one value. That is only sound because
[`Rotation`] and [`FontSize`] refuse non-finite values and normalize `-0.0`
at construction; a bare `f64` field here would make `Hash` and `PartialEq`
disagree.

is: `schema.ts` accepts any string, the toolbar writes a small fixed list,
and turning the field into an enum would refuse documents that open today.

ReadGetRangeOutput_FontSize.description:
A font size in points.

# The one place this is stricter than TypeScript

`schema.ts`'s validator is `typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v)` —
so `fontSize: 0` and `fontSize: -8` are *accepted* by the importer. Neither
renders as anything, and neither survives an edit: `isEmptyFormat` treats
`0` as falsy, so the first format touch on such a cell deletes the whole
record.

This type refuses both. Nothing is lost, because the wire reader
([`super::wire`]) drops a non-positive size to absence rather than failing
the load — the identical outcome to the collapse the TypeScript already
performs, reached deliberately instead of by accident.

ReadGetRangeOutput_CellBorders.description:
A cell's borders — any **non-empty** subset of the four edges.

# Why non-emptiness is a type invariant here

In TypeScript this is `Partial<Record<BorderSide, BorderEdge>>`, and `{}`
is a perfectly good value of that type. Three separate things then conspire
to keep it out of a document:

- the borders op collapses an edge-less result to `undefined`
  (`capabilities/format/borders.ts`);
- `format.ts` documents the consequence — "Never stored empty (`{}`) … so a
  present `borders` is truthy and correctly keeps the format";
- `schema.ts`'s `isCellBorders` rejects `{}` on import.

Three enforcement points for one invariant, in three files, none of which
the type mentions. Here [`CellBorders::new`] is the only constructor and it
refuses an empty set, so a `CellBorders` that exists has at least one edge —
which is exactly the premise
[`CellFormat::is_empty`](super::CellFormat::is_empty) relies on.

Fields are declared in the order the wire sorts them. That is documentation,
not mechanism: [`canonical`](crate::document::canonical) sorts keys on the
way out, so the bytes do not depend on this declaration order. A test pins
the emitted order anyway.

the emitted order anyway.

ReadGetConditionalFormatsOutput_Color.description:
A CSS colour string — `#ff0000`, `#fff2cc`, `rgb(…)`, a named colour.

# Why this is not a parsed colour

`schema.ts`'s validator for `color`/`fill` is `typeof v === 'string'`, full
stop. Studio's own writers only ever emit `#rrggbb`, and its
conditional-format wire validator *does* enforce a `HEX_COLOR` pattern —
but the plain cell format's does not, and a document containing
`color: "rebeccapurple"` loads today.

Parsing to an RGB triple here would therefore make documents that open stop
opening, and would re-serialize `"#FF0000"` as `"#ff0000"` — different
canonical bytes for a document nobody edited. So this is a validated
*string*, and the one thing it rejects is the empty string, which is not a
colour and which TypeScript only ever tolerated because
`isEmptyFormat` treated it as "no colour at all" (see
[`CellFormat::is_empty`](super::CellFormat::is_empty)).

ReadGetConditionalFormatsOutput_Decimals.description:
A fixed decimal-place count for a [`NumberFormat`].

# `Decimals(0)` is a value, not an absence

This is the type that carries the port's one deliberate behaviour change.
In TypeScript `decimals` is `number | undefined` and
`isEmptyFormat` — `Object.values(f).every(v => !v)` — reads `0` as falsy, so
setting zero decimal places on an otherwise-unformatted cell deletes the
cell's whole format record and the cell falls back to **automatic, which is
two decimal places**. Studio's own write-observer classifies that as
`blocked` and calls it "the exact false success R10 names"
(`api-contract/src/observe-writes.ts:280-320`).

`Option<Decimals>` cannot express that confusion: `Some(Decimals(0))` and
`None` are different values, and reproducing the collapse would mean writing
it deliberately. See [`CellFormat::is_empty`](super::CellFormat::is_empty)
for the full decision.

ReadGetConditionalFormatsOutput_Rotation.description:
Text rotation in degrees: positive tilts counter-clockwise (Sheets' "up"),
negative clockwise ("down").

`0` is the identity and is **not** a distinguishable state — `format.ts`
says so outright ("`undefined` (or `0`) = no rotation"), so
[`CellFormat`](super::CellFormat) normalizes it away rather than storing a
rotation of nothing.

# Why `f64` and not an integer

Sheets' UI only offers whole degrees and five presets (±45, ±90, 0), so an
`i8` is tempting and would make this type `Copy + Eq + Hash` for free.
`schema.ts`'s validator is `Number.isFinite(v) && v >= -90 && v <= 90`,
though — **not** `Number.isInteger` — so a document carrying `rotation:
45.5` loads today, and an `i8` port would refuse to open it. Narrowing an
accept-set is a migration, not a translation.

ReadGetConditionalFormatsOutput_HexColor.description:
A strictly-validated `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa` hex colour — `schema.ts`'s
own `HEX_COLOR = /^#([0-9a-fA-F]{3}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{8})$/`,
transcribed field for field rather than assumed from either capability
module.

# Why this is not [`Color`]

[`Color`] is deliberately loose — `schema.ts`'s plain per-cell
`color`/`fill` validator is `typeof v === 'string'`, full stop (see its own
doc). Banding/conditional-format's colours are validated by a genuinely
stricter wire rule, cited by `schema.ts` itself as shared by both
`set-conditional-format` and `set-banded-range`. Reusing [`Color`] here
would silently accept a document `schema.ts` rejects on the way in (e.g.
`"headerColor": "red"`) — this type exists so that mistake is a compile
error, not a divergence discovered by a fuzzer.
